title: Farmers Markets Are a Waste of Time for Small-Scale Farmers
body: I'm in my first full-time job at a farm and I've been helping out at our local farmers market. To be honest, after crunching some numbers, I think it's a money loser for us. Rent, table space, and all the other fees add up fast. We make maybe 10% profit on what we sell there, which is less than selling wholesale to restaurants or stores. And it's exhausting, especially when it rains or it's hot. Maybe I'm just not seeing something, but from where I sit, the returns aren't worth the effort.

title: Emergency Fund on a Shoestring Budget
body: When I first started teaching, my husband and I were living paycheck to paycheck. We had no savings at all, let alone an emergency fund. But we knew we needed something in case of unexpected expenses. So we started by setting aside $10 from each paycheck. It was tiny, but it added up over time. After a few months, we increased the amount and eventually built up enough for 3-6 months' worth of living expenses. That gave us peace of mind during uncertain times and allowed us to weather any financial storms that came our way.

title: Farming needs a reality check when it comes to getting young people involved.
body: I've been farming for over 20 years and I'm convinced that we're doing it all wrong. We expect kids to come back to the farm, but we don't give them a reason to stay. My own kids wouldn't last a day on this land if they had to do what their grandparents did. The work is too hard, the pay is too low, and the hours are too long. Until we make farming more appealing to young people, with better wages and more flexibility, we'll just be waiting for an older generation to retire.
